Probability-paper data for examining a similar exposure group (UNE-EN 689)

Source: R/une689_probability.R
une689_probability_data.Rd

Computes the quantities needed to draw the graphical validation of a similar exposure group (SEG, "GES" in Spanish) on probability paper: the daily exposure values are ranked in ascending order and each rank k is assigned the plotting position \(P_k = (k - 3/8) / (n + 1/4)\). If the data follow the assumed distribution, the points fall approximately on a straight line when plotted against \(P_k\) on log-normal paper (lognormal data) or on normal paper (normal data).

Usage

une689_probability_data(
  ed,
  distribution = c("auto", "lognormal", "normal"),
  alpha = 0.05
)

Arguments

ed

Numeric vector. Daily exposure (ED) values, all strictly positive; between 3 and 5000 values.

distribution

Character. "lognormal", "normal", or "auto" (default). With "auto" the lognormal distribution is used if the Shapiro-Wilk test on log(ED) does not reject it at level alpha; otherwise the normal distribution is used if the test on ED does not reject it; if both are rejected, an error is raised. The labels returned by une689_distribution_type() (English or Spanish) are also accepted.

alpha

Numeric. Significance level of the Shapiro-Wilk tests used by distribution = "auto" (default 0.05).

Value

A list with elements:

data

A data.frame with one row per observation and columns k (rank), ed (sorted values), pk (plotting position), pk_percent (100 * pk), z (standard normal quantile of pk), y (log(ed) for lognormal, ed for normal), fitted and residual of the straight-line fit.

distribution

"lognormal" or "normal".

n

Number of observations.

intercept, slope

Coefficients of the straight line y = intercept + slope * z.

r_squared

Coefficient of determination of the fit.

W, p_value

Shapiro-Wilk statistic and p-value for the chosen distribution (on log(ed) for lognormal, on ed for normal).

alpha

The significance level used.

Details

The vertical coordinate used for the fit is the standard normal quantile \(z_k = \Phi^{-1}(P_k)\), which is what the probability scale of the paper represents. The straight line is the least-squares regression of log(ED) (lognormal) or ED (normal) on \(z_k\). For lognormal data the intercept and slope estimate log(MG) and log(DSG), and for normal data they estimate MA and DS; these are regression-based graphical estimates and do not replace une689_statistics().

The coefficient of determination returned in r_squared is purely descriptive. The graphical check is a visual one: the group is considered consistent when all points lie close to a straight line and none is exceptionally separated from the rest. This function does not apply any numerical cut-off to that judgement.

Note that stats::ppoints() uses the same plotting positions only for n <= 10; this function always uses \((k - 3/8)/(n + 1/4)\).

See also

une689_probability_plot(), une689_normality_test(), une689_distribution_type()

Examples

ed <- c(0.008, 0.012, 0.017, 0.021, 0.034, 0.041)
pd <- une689_probability_data(ed)
pd$distribution
#> [1] "lognormal"
pd$data[, c("k", "ed", "pk")]
#>   k    ed   pk
#> 1 1 0.008 0.10
#> 2 2 0.012 0.26
#> 3 3 0.017 0.42
#> 4 4 0.021 0.58
#> 5 5 0.034 0.74
#> 6 6 0.041 0.90
pd$r_squared
#> [1] 0.9825294
